policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Aorist ἀπειθήσαντες vs present ἀπειθοῦντες; ASV 'the Jews that were disobedient' is a stative English rendering that carries neither aspect. No note. Underdetermined.

ASV 'speaking boldly in the Lord' renders παρρησιαζόμενοι with a dative complement equally well whether ἐπί is present or the dative stands alone; the preposition leaves no separate English reflex. Underdetermined.
Word order of the periphrastic εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἦσαν only; 'and there they preached the gospel' cannot register it. The note is a cross-reference on the gospel idiom, not a variant. Underdetermined.
Word order of ἀδύνατος and ἐν Λύστροις only; ASV fronts 'And at Lystra' as normal English clause order, which reflects no Greek sequence. Underdetermined.
The added participle ὑπάρχων is a copular redundancy with χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ that ASV's 'a cripple from his mother’s womb' would leave untranslated either way. Underdetermined.

Aorist περιεπάτησεν vs pluperfect περιπεπατήκει; ASV 'who never had walked' uses the ordinary English past perfect for a relative clause anterior to past narrative, which ASV supplies for a Greek aorist as freely as for a pluperfect. Underdetermined.

Aorist ἤκουσεν vs imperfect ἤκουεν; ASV 'The same heard Paul speaking' shows the ongoing action in the participle, not in the finite verb, so the aspect of the verb is not distinguished. Underdetermined.
Word order of ἔχει and πίστιν only; 'that he had faith to be made whole' is fixed English order. Underdetermined.
Presence of the article τῇ with μεγάλῃ in the dative phrase; ASV 'with a loud voice' uses the English indefinite idiom for the phrase regardless. Underdetermined.
Predicate adjective ὀρθός vs adverb ὀρθῶς; English 'upright' in 'Stand upright on thy feet' is itself ambiguous between the two and does not distinguish them. Underdetermined.
Aorist ἥλατο vs imperfect ἥλλετο; ASV's simple past 'he leaped up' carries no aspectual marking. Underdetermined.
Connective τε vs δέ; ASV's narrative 'And when the multitude saw' is its standard rendering for either. Underdetermined.
Article ὁ with the proper name Παῦλος; ASV renders the personal name 'Paul' identically with or without the article. Underdetermined.

Addition of correlative μέν; ASV's 'And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercury' leaves μέν untranslated as it regularly does, so the English does not distinguish it. Notes here are Greek glosses on the divine names. Underdetermined.
Connective τε vs δέ; ASV's opening 'And the priest' fits either. Underdetermined.

ASV reads 'whose temple was before the city' with no possessive. The RP addition αὐτῶν would give 'before their city', and ASV renders such a genitive pronoun; its absence in the English selects the shorter reading.
αὐτῶν vs reflexive ἑαυτῶν with τὰ ἱμάτια; ASV 'their garments' renders both alike. Underdetermined.
ASV 'sprang forth among the multitude' renders the ἐκ- compound ἐξεπήδησαν; the RP εἰσεπήδησαν ('sprang in', as KJV 'ran in among the people') is excluded by the directional force of 'forth'.

ASV 'unto a living God' is indefinite, rendering anarthrous θεὸν ζῶντα; the RP articular τὸν θεὸν τὸν ζῶντα would give 'the living God'. The English article selects the base reading. The verse note is an alternative_rendering on 'passions' and does not bear here.
καίτοι vs καίτοιγε; the enclitic γε adds no separable English reflex and ASV renders 'And yet' either way. Underdetermined.
Orthographic and reflexive variation among αὑτόν, ἑαυτόν, αὐτόν; all three yield ASV 'himself'. Underdetermined.
ἀγαθουργῶν vs ἀγαθοποιῶν, synonymous compounds both rendered by ASV 'in that he did good'. Underdetermined.
ASV 'filling your hearts with food and gladness' renders the second-person ὑμῶν, matching 'gave you from heaven' earlier in the verse; the RP first-person ἡμῶν ('our hearts') is excluded.
Present νομίζοντες vs aorist νομίσαντες; ASV's participle 'supposing that he was dead' carries no aspectual distinction. Underdetermined.
Word order of τῶν μαθητῶν and αὐτόν only; 'as the disciples stood round about him' is fixed English order. Underdetermined.
ASV repeats the preposition — 'to Lystra, and to Iconium, and to Antioch' — matching the repeated εἰς of the base reading; the RP omission would give a single governing preposition over the series.
ASV repeats the preposition — 'to Lystra, and to Iconium, and to Antioch' — matching the repeated εἰς of the base reading; the RP omission would give a single governing preposition over the series.
Word order of πρεσβυτέρους and κατ᾽ ἐκκλησίαν only; ASV 'elders in every church' is fixed English order. Underdetermined.
Article τήν with the place name Πισιδίαν; ASV 'through Pisidia' takes no article for a proper place name either way. Underdetermined.
Imperfect ἀνήγγελλον vs aorist ἀνήγγειλαν; ASV's simple past 'they rehearsed' carries no aspectual marking. Underdetermined.

ASV 'And they tarried no little time with the disciples' has no adverb of place. The RP addition ἐκεῖ would give 'there', which ASV renders explicitly elsewhere (14:7 'and there they preached'); its absence selects the base reading.
